site_summary: Live-table pressure, player follow-up, and GM-approved world fallout for Chummer6.

editorial_posture.opening: Start with the person at the table, not the system diagram. Chummer6 is strongest when a player can build a runner, understand the choices, give that runner a past, and then watch the campaign remember the consequences without stealing authority from the GM.
editorial_posture.source_note: This guide follows the Chummer6 design canon and the public-guide source set. Treat it as a product guide, not as a rules engine or an unbounded release promise.

overview.title: Chummer6 At The Table
overview.purpose: Explain the Chummer6 live-play and living-world stack in plain product language for players, GMs, and curious visitors.
overview.one_line_pitch: Chummer6 turns live table pressure, between-session faction motion, and public-safe world fallout into one governed play loop where the GM stays in charge and every meaningful action leaves a receipt.
overview.delivery_posture: Use this as the presentation story for the workbench plus campaign layer. Some surfaces are live and some are target shape; the guide keeps that boundary visible without making the reader decode internal release evidence.
system_truths: all public fallout is public-safe and approval-gated
media tools may dramatize or suggest, but they do not become truth on their own

surfaces.name: Player Action Cards
feels: connected to the city, not just the session transcript

surfaces.name: Living Newsroom
must_never_imply: the event was invented after the fact

play_loop.name: Spark
play_loop.description: A session event raises heat and creates a bounded pulse packet with typed context and recipient rules.

play_loop.name: Reach
play_loop.description: If policy and consent allow it, the pulse packet becomes player-facing or faction-facing delivery.

play_loop.name: Response
play_loop.description: Players or factions respond inside governed rails.

play_loop.name: Fallout
play_loop.description: Enough validated response can produce public-safe fallout.

comes_from: watching a player action card cascade into faction consequences
seeing Passport identity, role path, and city pressure connect
watching a remote reaction mini-game end in a newsroom or public-safe city fallout beat

hero_moment: a run spikes heat and the GM approves a bounded pulse packet
a player receives an action card with one sharp risky choice and one safer choice
the choice resolves into Passport movement, faction pressure, and a receipt trail
the city later reflects that action through rumor, newsroom fallout, or public-safe consequence
hard_truths: remote reactions are mini-games, not direct table mutation
public projection requires public-safe GM-approved posture
BeHuman and Answerly stay adapter layers
flagship_bar: player action cards, Passport, and GM cockpit all exist as coherent product surfaces.
Remote reaction mini-games are real moments a player can understand and answer.
Inbox, rumor, order, and fallout lanes are receipt-backed.
Public-safe projection stays bounded by GM authority.
The system still feels fast, legible, and exciting for players.

product_taxonomy.title: What Belongs Where
product_taxonomy.summary: Chummer6 should read like one product with a strong core and a few ambitious expansion bets. If a user needs it to build, understand, run, remember, or return to a campaign, it belongs in the product story. The future shelf is only for the larger bets that still need distance from today’s download.

base_features.name: Workbench
base_features.description: the dense character-building surface, inspectors, source detail, compare views, and release packaging that make Chummer feel credible to existing users first.

base_features.name: ALICE
base_features.description: the in-product build mentor and rules explainer; it is a normal workbench feature, not a separate future promise.

base_features.name: Origin Dossier
base_features.description: the origin-and-life-behind-the-stats feature; it belongs beside ALICE as an emotional entry into the runner, not as a distant idea shelf.

base_features.name: NEXUS-PAN
base_features.description: the continuity and recovery feature for shared state, reconnects, and device drift; it should feel like reliability, not a future brand.

base_features.name: Ready for Tonight
base_features.description: the practical return-to-play surface that helps a GM or player know what is ready before a session.

base_features.name: Runner Passport
base_features.description: the runner identity and continuity surface that follows the character from build into campaign life.

base_features.name: Knowledge Fabric
base_features.description: the source-aware rules explanation layer that makes values, legality, and tradeoffs traceable.

base_features.name: Table Pulse and GM Cockpit
base_features.description: campaign-operation features for heat, reaction cards, approvals, and aftermath; they should be presented as the campaign layer, not as a random new brand.

future_horizons.name: Karma Forge
future_horizons.description: governed house-rule and package evolution; it remains a Horizon because it changes how tables extend the rules.

future_horizons.name: Black Ledger
future_horizons.description: living city, faction motion, public-safe news, and world-tick projection; it is the biggest campaign expansion bet.

future_horizons.name: Runbook Press and Creator OS
future_horizons.description: campaign publishing and creator output; together they are one publish/share expansion, not two competing shelves.

future_horizons.name: Community Hub and Jackpoint
future_horizons.description: community, open-run, dossier, and recap collaboration; together they are the social/campaign-memory expansion.

future_horizons.name: Runsite, Ghostwire, and Anarchy
future_horizons.description: specialized play modes for spatial prep, replay/forensics, and rules-light sessions; useful, but not first-minute product identity.

throw_out.name: Onramp
throw_out.reason: Onramp is starter help. Keep it inside the first-session path instead of promoting it as a separate product bet.

throw_out.name: Quicksilver as a headline Horizon
throw_out.reason: Quicksilver is navigation and command-deck polish. It should support the product, not compete with the product story.

throw_out.name: Local Co-Processor as a public promise
throw_out.reason: Local acceleration is infrastructure. Keep it in technical docs until a user-facing need makes it worth naming.

minigames.title: Table Pulse Remote Reaction Minigames
minigames.purpose: Remote reaction mini-games give players a short, dramatic way to answer the city between sessions without turning side moments into unapproved campaign truth.
minigames.goal: Give players a dramatic city-is-still-moving moment without breaking consent, authority, or campaign privacy.

families.name: Intercept
families.description: The player receives a short intelligence or courier card and chooses how aggressively to intercept, forward, or suppress it.

families.name: Cover Story
families.description: The player gets a social or public-facing cleanup card and must pick a cover approach.
payoff: possible contradiction receipt for later review

families.name: Scramble
families.description: The player gets a time-sensitive logistics or support card.

families.name: Temptation
families.description: The player gets a morally gray opportunity card.

families.name: Shadow Reply
families.description: A player or faction representative sends back a coded answer to a pulse packet.

may_not: create public truth on their own
reveal private session content by default

must_show: whether the GM must still approve fallout

player_action_cards: one strong dramatic choice and one safer choice

wow_pattern: a player gets a tight dramatic card
the choice feels sharp and immediate
the result lands in Passport or faction pressure
the city later reflects that move through rumor or newsroom fallout
anti_pattern: a random mini-quiz disconnected from world state
minigames.example_loop: After a high-heat extraction, a player receives a Scramble mini-game as a short action card. They choose to burn a favor to reroute a courier instead of going dark. That choice creates a receipt, nudges a faction pressure lane, preserves one standing-order asset, and later lets the newsroom surface show a subtle public-safe consequence instead of exposing the whole private session.
flagship_bar: the card is dramatic in under one screen
the choice is meaningful but bounded
the result can feed Passport, rumor, faction, or newsroom lanes
the system still keeps GM and consent authority intact

user_first_story.title: User-First Entry Arc
user_first_story.summary: The flagship story no longer starts only with table heat. A player can begin with a grounded origin dossier, approve canon, let ALICE use that canon as bounded build-help context, and then carry that identity into Passport, player action cards, and the living-world stack.
beats: A player starts from Origin Dossier instead of facing a cold chargen sheet.
Approved canon freezes a stable narrative spine before downstream media regenerates.
ALICE uses the approved canon later as bounded context for build help, rules coach follow-up, and GM-steered tradeoff explanation.
Table Pulse, Runner Passport, and the living newsroom then make that runner feel present in a governed city instead of trapped in a one-session character form.
truths: approved origin canon may shape later ALICE suggestions
GM gimmicks and allowances may steer narrative context without becoming auto-applied mechanics
media packets derive from canon and receipts, not the other way around
ALICE remains advisory and explainable even when the origin lane is rich and cinematic

origin_dossier_spotlight.title: Origin Dossier And ALICE
origin_dossier_spotlight.summary: Origin Dossier should now read as a flagship base feature: a player enters Chummer as a runner with causes, debts, people, scars, secrets, and unfinished consequences. ALICE keeps that story connected to rules explanation without letting prose silently mutate build truth.
must_show: blank-state start and finished-runner additive entry points
bundle root and derivative dossier media outputs
voice-selection posture before audiobook packet generation
bounded GM gimmick steering as advisory context
later ALICE follow-up that references approved canon instead of inventing a new story spine
alice_connection: ALICE owns the native desktop workbench for Build Help, Rules Coach, and Origin Dossier.
Origin Dossier may start before chargen or from an already-finished runner without forcing mechanics back into edit mode.
The approved origin canon feeds later ALICE explanations about tradeoffs, upgrades, and risk.
GM allowances may appear in ALICE context and output, but they must not silently rewrite mechanics.
Narration lanes should expose voice posture as an explicit user choice, not an invisible provider default.
The lane is strongest when narrative continuity and rules explanation stay on the same governed rail.
must_not_imply: origin prose becomes mechanical truth by itself
downstream portrait or video providers become rules authority
ALICE is an autonomous build oracle

gm_cockpit_spotlight.title: GM Cockpit And Steering
gm_cockpit_spotlight.summary: GM Cockpit is the calm authority surface for steering Table Pulse, origin-dossier context, remote reactions, and public-safe fallout without turning a maintenance list into the product experience.
must_show: recipient reasoning, quiet-hours, mute, and opt-out posture
GM allowances and gimmicks as explicit advisory context
mini-game card source, chosen response, and proposed consequence
public-safe release controls before any newsroom or public map projection
receipt trail, override reason, and what remains manual review
origin_gimmick_flow: GM steer may come before the origin story so it can shape tone, faction pressure, and allowed context.
The fixed SR4 troll decker test gimmick is a clinic contact that fronts restricted starter ware and one over-availability deck part.
ALICE may explain how that changes story pressure, legality posture, availability risk, and ware consequences.
The cockpit must keep those allowances advisory until a GM or player explicitly applies legal mechanics in the normal character workflow.
visual_language: control room, action board, pressure map, and dossier drawer rather than admin table
dense but scannable cards for heat, consent, receipt, and consequence state
one strong primary action for adjudicate, approve, suppress, or request revision
must_not_imply: the GM cockpit is an autonomous simulator
GM gimmicks auto-apply ware, money, gear, qualities, or availability exceptions
public media can bypass private campaign posture or GM approval
